title: Runbook gaps & follow-ups: night shift
body:
Shift summary (23 Mar 2026, 22:00-06:00 PT)

Quick note: fairly noisy night due to two related capacity/latency events on hosted-api-west1. No full outage, but multiple pages and client retries. Kept service degradations contained via temporary routing and scaled pools. Notes below are messy — meant for handoff + action items for next-day follow-ups.

Timeline & pages:
- 22:13: page from prod-alerts: hosted-api-west1 95th latency > 500ms for 10m (alerts/latency-95). Pager: me.
- 22:17: spike continued, error-rate increase small (~0.3%). Began digging: dashboard showed increased tail (p99) and consistent CPU hot on a subset of GPU instances.
- 22:25: routed ~30% traffic to hosted-api-east as temporary mitigation (routing override). Latency dropped to baseline by 22:33.
- 23:08: second page — ephemeral failures on embeddings endpoint for short bursts (JIRA-4521). Correlated with a batch job from infra running large embedding backfill.

Initial troubleshooting notes:
- Hypothesis: sudden change in request size distribution (longer sequences) + insufficient autoscale/burst capacity on west1 pool. Batching/queueing in runtime increased latency for other requests.
- Command checks run:
  * kubectl get pods -n hosted-west -o wide | grep gpu-pool-
  * curl -s "https://internal-metrics/api?metric=runtime_queue_depth&region=west1"
  * gcloud compute instances list --filter="name~'west1-gpu'"
- Observed one node with repeated OOM-kernel messages in node logs (investigate further — may be driver/kernel mismatch). Logged node id: i-west-03-7a.

Mitigations taken:
- Applied routing override to shift 30% traffic to east1 (config: routing/overrides/2026-03-23-night).
- Temporarily increased burst capacity for west1 pool by +2 nodes (not ideal long-term).
- Kicked off embedding backfill pause (infra-runbooks -> pause-job JIRA-4523).

Runbook gaps discovered (to capture & fix):
1) No clear play for "partial tail latency due to homogeneous large-sequence requests". Current runbook covers scale and full pool failure but not sequence-length-driven queuing. Needs a diagnostic checklist and commands to quickly identify per-model sequence distribution.
   - Suggested addition: quick query to request-logs to plot sequence_length histogram last 15m. Example query stub (ELK):
     POST /_search
     {"query": {"bool": {"must": [{"match": {"region": "west1"}}, {"range": {"@timestamp": {"gte": "now-15m"}}}]}, "aggs": {"seq_len": {"histogram": {"field": "request.seq_len", "interval": 32}}}}

2) Runbook lacks clear guidance for when to route by "cost-tier/latency-sensitivity" vs. purely by region. For tonight we used a blunt region shift; we should document criteria and the small step commands to move only low-latency-sensitive routes.

3) Node-level driver/kernel mismatch detection: we had one node with repeated OOM/driver restarts. Runbook should include: exact log grep pattern, safe cordon/drain sequence for GPU nodes (avoid killing KV caches), and automated incident tag for infra.

Follow-up action items (owner / ETA):
- Rachel: draft runbook section for sequence-length diagnostics + example ELK query and CLIs. ETA: 2026-03-25 morning.
- Priya: add dashboard panels for request.seq_len histogram in per-region latency dashboard. ETA: 2026-03-26.
- Miguel: check node i-west-03-7a driver version and validate against current AMI. File infra ticket if mismatch. ETA: 2026-03-24 EOD. (Linked: JIRA-4523)
- SRE rotation: add a short note to the oncall checklist to check batch jobs/backfills scheduled for the region at shift start. Owner: oncall playbook page update. ETA: 2026-03-27.

Short-term tactical TODOs (things I left undone / next-shift):
- Add a one-liner to routing override docs showing how to target routes by tag (low_latency_sensitive:false) — I did manual override; should be easier.
- Follow up with infra about kernel oops on i-west-03-7a and whether that node should be quarantined.
- Re-run a small synthetic load against west1 with long sequences to reproduce and capture tracing (x-ray). I left a curl script at ~/oncall/sim-longseq.sh — next person can run (requires dev creds).

Notes for postmortem (if we escalate):
- Timeline of events + decision to route traffic (include timestamps above).
- Root cause candidates: request-size distribution shift + one degraded node causing head-of-line blocking in batch queues.
- Impact: small error-rate bump, tail latency increase, some client retries, no dropped SLAs.
- Remediation proposals: sequence-length-aware admission control OR per-model shaping; add kv cache warmup/priority for small requests; infra: ensure driver/kernel alignment and node retirement automation.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did autoscaler not add capacity earlier than manual +2 nodes? Check autoscaler logs and policy thresholds (scale-up cooldown?).
- Does runtime expose per-model queuing metrics? If not, add proposal to product to surface per-model queue depth.
- Which customers were affected? Need to correlate with client-id in request logs. I started a query (JIRA-4521) but didn't finish mapping to account ids.

Handoff bullet points for morning oncall:
- Check JIRA-4521 (latency pages) updates; if still open, re-run the ELK seq_len query and check the last 30m.
- Verify i-west-03-7a status (Miguel has the ticket). If it reboots/ooms again, cordon and replace.
- Remove routing override only after p95 and p99 back to baseline for 30m.

Random notes to myself:
- Remember to add "sequence_length" to the synthetic user agent generator for load tests.
- Consider adding an automated runbook test that intentionally runs a long-sequence request against a canary to ensure per-region autoscale behavior.

-- Rachel
